correspondence.finding: The selected short opening and northward turn correspond at ordinary component scale to the drainage west of Jaçanã, in the mapped Rch. da Areia setting. The route continues north past the western side of Coronel Ezequiel. An exact spring and the name of the entire initial short branch remain unassigned.

The mapped local feeder network continues northeast past Tábua do Meio/Tábua de Baixo into the Santa Catarina impoundment setting, then toward the Campo Redondo/Santa Cruz side. The publications distinguish Rch. Papagaio da Tábua, Rch. Fechado, Rch. da Chova and Rch. do Salgado local approaches; none is promoted to a uniform representative name. The separately depicted western feeder impoundment is not a required passage of the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Rio Trairi and Santa Cruz reservoir
correspondence.finding: The northeast course near Bom Jesus, Passagem do Meio, Vazante and Jacaracica is explicitly labelled Rio Trairi and connects into Açude Público Santa Cruz immediately west of Santa Cruz. The selected continuation turns south through the city/river corridor. Açude Bom Jardim and the more northern Rio Inharé approach are separate mapped components.

Southbound Rio Trairi passes the Santana/Umbuzeiro-side setting. Açude do Umbuzeiro and Rio São Francisco approach from the west are depicted separately; no full traversal of Umbuzeiro reservoir is inferred. The selected route continues south, then turns east past Tanque and the Volta/Tubira/Voltas Tubibas/Umari corridor toward the principal Trairi reservoir.

The selected western incoming river reaches the western reservoir arm, crosses the mapped Açude Público Trairi body and leaves at the northern end near Guarita before turning east/north toward Tangará. Southern reservoir arms and nearby Açude Guarita/Arapuá are not renamed as the selected mainstem.

The mapped outgoing Rio Trairi bends north, northeast and east through Tangará, Poço Cercado, Cacimba de Baixo and Boa Saúde/Januário Cicco. Its eastern continuation is distinguished from the Jacu and Jacu-Mirim corridors farther south.

The regional original maps the complete selected eastward and northern bend toward Monte Alegre and onward southeast to São José de Mipibu/Nísia Floresta. Rio Trairi is labelled on this receiving trunk. The southern Rio Arari is a separate joining approach, rather than the name of the whole selected line.

The lower Trairi reaches the western Lagoa Papary setting; separate Rio Arari approaches from the southwest. Original municipal mapping depicts the east/southeast lake-and-channel continuation into the Papeba setting and the southward connection toward Guaraíras. Nearby Lagoa do Bonfim, Papebinha, aquaculture areas and coastal lakes are not silently included in the selected group.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Lagoa de Guaraíras and downstream Atlantic inlet
correspondence.finding: The final selected segment corresponds to the northern Guaraíras receiving-lagoon arm beside Senador Georgino Avelino. The original maps show its connection southward into the wider lagoon and the separate Atlantic opening by Tibau. The retained sea-terminal metadata does not establish that the selected rendered endpoint itself is at the open-ocean mouth. No geometry change is proposed.

correspondence.component_scope: Western opening and wetland-bearing upper channel
correspondence.finding: The selected western start is on the north/northeast-running channel among low relief west of Lago Lynch. It turns east, then southeast into the upper Grande corridor. The historical 500k original labels this approach Río Zapata; the finer MMA original labels the same upper channel Río Grande and shows the separate Río Donoso tributary entering from the southwest. Continental-wetland polygons occur along and beside the opening and the upper eastward route.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at ordinary headwater and channel-corridor scale. The full initial course and eastward connector are positively depicted on the 500k original, complementing the finer hydrography; no exact spring or channel-tip agreement is claimed.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Mapped continental wetlands, with many unknown polygon names retained null. No selected lake or reservoir traversal is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper meanders and Río Japón junction
correspondence.finding: East of the Donoso joining area the selected trunk bends southeast and then east/northeast along the southern side of a wetland tract. The historical original shows Río Japón arriving from the northwest/north and joining the channel labeled Río Grande. Finer MMA mapping supplies the additional northern tributary convergence in this same corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the meanders, the Japón/northern-branch joining setting and the continuation to the major southern bend.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Wetland tract alongside the upper meanders; not a lake traversal or separate terminal basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Lago Lynch–Riveros and Lago Blanco tributary links
correspondence.finding: The selected Grande bends south and then east where the separately mapped northeast-draining outlet corridor of Lago Lynch joins from the southwest. MMA labels the joining tributary Río Riveros. Farther east the historical original depicts the northward outlet of Lago Blanco joining the selected Grande at its next southern bend; another substantial southern tributary joins before the frontier approach. These are side contributions to the selected trunk, not model travel through Lynch or Blanco.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at lake-outlet, confluence and trunk-corridor scale on the original 500k map and finer middle MMA view. The official prose independently confirms contributions from both lake outlets.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Natural lake-fed tributary links are material context. Both named lakes lie off the selected retained path; their names are not extended to the river or all feeders. No reservoir passage is shown.

correspondence.component_scope: International border transition and Argentina upper valley
correspondence.finding: The meandering trunk continues east across the Chile–Argentina boundary and along the valley north of Estancia Aurelia. The original topography distinguishes the border-crossing Grande from northern Herminita and the southern Bella Vista tributary approaches. Wet valley-floor/floodplain symbols accompany the river.
correspondence.correspondence: Established across the international transition and both sides of the frontier; border and name association alone are not the evidence, because original channel geography is directly read.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Nearby lakes and wet depressions remain distinct from the selected main channel. No intervening lake/reservoir crossing is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle/lower Argentina tributary convergence and floodplain
correspondence.finding: The original follows the selected Grande east/northeast through the broad meandering floodplain past Aurelia, with southern tributary valleys, northern Moneta drainage and the Candelaria approach visible before the widening lower river. The official report identifies the tributary sequence as de la Turba and Mac Lennan from the south, Moneta from the north south of Estancia M. Behety, and final Candelaria from the south. That prose-only Mac Lennan name is kept distinct from directly read map labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Established through the complete selected lower channel corridor and material joining settings. The narrower tributary names do not become names for the trunk.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Numerous adjacent lagunas and marsh/floodplain areas are mapped. The selected route remains in the Grande channel rather than traversing those neighboring lake interiors.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Atlantic estuarine terminal beside Río Grande city
correspondence.finding: Downstream of the final southern tributary the mapped river broadens into a winding estuary beside Río Grande city, passes the El Tropezón/J. Menéndez vicinity and opens to the Atlantic coast at Punta Popper. The retained terminal belongs to this coastal estuary/mouth setting. The original map, rather than the model sea classification alone, establishes the open-coast outlet.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at generalized estuary and coastal-opening scale. Exact tidal bank, present-day spit shape or mouth point is not claimed.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Tidal/estuarine terminal, distinct from nearby Cabo Peñas and San Luis lagoons. No artificial impoundment is inferred.

correspondence.finding: The initial selected sector lies in a field of unnamed lakes and short channels, continuing southeast toward the adjoining Tavani sheet. The source distinguishes individual waterbodies; no hydronym is printed for the selected feeder. The selected initial headward-lake transfer has not been established as a continuous mapped connection.

The map depicts the eastward approach among small unnamed lakes and the larger lake complex at the southern turn, with short channels and rapids. The turn toward the next northern lake chain is in part crossed by a thick thematic boundary. A complete selected through-transfer is not established from the readable generalized mapping.

correspondence.component_scope: Across the Tavani/Gibson Lake sheet boundary
correspondence.finding: Both sheets show successive elongated lakes, bays, narrow channels and adjacent separate waters across this sector. Their occurrence and sheet-to-sheet setting are directly read. The entire selected northward transfer among these waters remains unresolved; neither proximity nor the model line is used to supply an unseen connector.

The broad selected sector turns northwest through lake-dotted uplands, with linked small channels and larger elongated lakes. Surrounding short branches and rapids are depicted. This provides local corridor context, but does not remove the unresolved upper transfer or establish one named river through every selected lake.

The original shows a multi-armed unnamed lake complex, northwestern/western channel approaches, a downstream junction with a more northerly feeder, and an eastward channel toward Gibson Lake. The distinct feeder and lake passages are retained as components; they are not renamed after Gibson Lake.

Gibson Lake is explicitly labelled on the original. The selected corridor traverses its northern part and northeast outlet setting, where the map shows rapids and a cabin. The lake label is not a scalar river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Gibson Lake outlet to western Barbour Bay
correspondence.finding: The short lower channel runs generally east, with narrow widened waters and rapids, and reaches the western head of Barbour Bay. The same original shows Barbour Bay opening northward to Chesterfield Inlet. The separate river entering from Hanway Lake to the south is not substituted for this selected western approach. No river hydronym is established for the selected outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward opening and lake/stream connectors
correspondence.finding: South of Mont D’Iberville and inside the divide from Labrador-facing streams, the selected opening occupies a small unnamed lake/outlet setting. The mapped stream runs southeast through the small-waterbody/notch setting before turning west into the Koroc valley. Original enlarged map pixels show the intervening blue stream links, rather than inferring the connection from basin shading.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary headward-component scale; small waterbody and feeder names null.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Koroc valley and southern bend
correspondence.finding: The east–west valley carries the printed Rivière Koroc label and receives short northern and southern tributaries. The selected route follows it west and then southwest around the terrain north of Mont Haywood; it remains distinct from the Palmer and Nakvak drainages across the Torngat divide. Narrow and locally split channels are mapped throughout this transition.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous selected valley and material turning reach read.

correspondence.finding: The north-side Ruisseau Naksarulak joins the westward Koroc. The selected route continues past the mapped Chute Korluktok setting, with split-channel/braid areas upstream and downstream. No lake-to-lake or basin-boundary shortcut is substituted for this valley.
correspondence.correspondence: Junction and intervening mapped river continuation read.

correspondence.finding: Ruisseau Sukaliuk approaches from the south and Rivière André-Grenier from the north, joining the Koroc in succession along the selected westward route. The original maps distinguish the joining valleys and widened/anastomosed river areas. The selected path does not continue upstream into these separate tributary systems or their named lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: Both material joins and their selected-mainstem connectors read.

correspondence.finding: The selected river follows the winding western Koroc valley, north of the separate Lac Amittuujaq/La Ralde setting, then turns northwest toward the coastal lowlands. Ruisseau Narsaaluk arrives from the east near the widening lower river. Numerous surrounding lakes belong to side drainages; the selected mainstem follows the mapped valley watercourse through the lowland terrain.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous lower river read; surrounding lake presence is not used as a substitute connector.

correspondence.finding: Beyond the Narsaaluk junction, the river widens into the mapped lower Koroc estuary and continues northwest toward Anse Tasiujakuluk on Ungava Bay. The actual selected terminal is read in this coastal receiving-water setting. Rivière George and Kangiqsualujjuaq lie to the south across intervening land and are not the selected receiving river.
correspondence.correspondence: Terminal-side river/estuary and open coastal relation established at corridor scale, without a surveyed mouth or tidal-line claim.
